# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.25 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.24. Written and tested by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; **nothing was tried on Windows, macOS or arm64** (the CI test suite runs on all three and was green for the last commit before this one, but nobody opened the window or ran a real scan there).

**New**
- **Page layout for columns of short lines** (poems, stanzas side by side): a line of text that crosses the gutter no longer hides it, and rows of stanza columns are read row by row. On 15 held-out brochure pages the error rate fell from 11.95 % to 6.01 % (two pages from 47–56 % to 3–4 %); the magazine test pages and five hand-transcribed pages of a 1960 textbook did not get worse.
- **Words end at wide gaps even when the network wrote no space.** Table cells used to come out glued (`CantitatePreț`) and tables were not found at all; a table with ruled lines now comes out as one table with the right cells (Excel: `--tables-xlsx`). A table without lines is still found as two tables (left half, right half): not solved. Cost: magazine test error 3.66 % → 3.73 % (mostly one halftone page), book pages 1.63 % → 1.58 %.
- **Romanian word list accepts the 1953–1993 spelling** (`cuvînt`, `romîn`, `sînt`): the 1960 textbook pages went from 99.6 % to 99.7 % of characters and 96.0 % to 96.3 % of words.
- `--clean-text`: a word broken across lines keeps its hyphen when both halves are listed words and the plain join is not (`social-` / `democrat`); `--cedilla` writes `ş ţ` instead of `ș ț`.
- `--drop-running-heads`: running heads, feet and page numbers that repeat on at least half of the pages (four pages minimum) are left out of the .txt and .docx text and listed on stderr.
- `--accurate`: every line read three times (shifted a pixel up and down), probabilities averaged. Slower (measured +18 % to +74 %); a gain only on the magazine pages (3.66 % → 3.39 %), none on books and brochures. Off by default.
- Speed: skew detection no longer scores the coarse angle grid twice; page preparation 0.64 s → 0.52 s on one test page, text identical.
- Earlier in this series, already in `main` but not in any release: EPUB 3 export (`--epub`), verify pack (`--verify-pack`), command palette and before/after slider in the window, text-diff page (`--diff-html`), sealed mode (`--offline`), SVG outlines (`--vectorize`). See the README.

**Fixed**
- Asking for a page past the end of a PDF (`book.pdf#9` of a 3-page file) returned the last page when `mutool` was the renderer; the page count is now checked first.

**Tried and not adopted** (numbers in ROADMAP 4.49–4.74): a model fine-tuned on two more digital books (better on three test sets, worse on the 1960 book once measured correctly), a language-model decoder (upper bound about 0.15 points), int8 network, display-title layout, a dense-line filter. The built-in model is the same as in pre.24.

**Not tried / unverified**: Windows, macOS, arm64; the window with real flagged pages for the new keys and filters; read-aloud with a real voice; EPUB with EPUBCheck; the new window texts are machine-written translations; `--drop-running-heads` and the hyphen rule have unit tests and one real page each, no benchmark.

**The guide PDF attached to this release is still the pre.21 text.**

**Known limits (unchanged)**: OCR can misread characters such as `@`; the rotation behaviour seen on Windows 11 is unconfirmed; the display title of a page with a halftone panel is lost.
